## ButtonVariant

```typescript
type ButtonVariant = "default" | "primary" | "danger" | "warn" | "quiet"
```

How a button reads.

`default` is a plain button, `primary` is the one action on the
panel, `danger` is the one that destroys something, `warn` says the
action is not what it sounds like, and `quiet` is a button that
should not be the first thing the eye lands on.

## ButtonSize

```typescript
type ButtonSize = "md" | "sm" | "xs"
```

`md` unless the row is dense, in which case `sm` or `xs`.

## ButtonProps

```typescript
interface ButtonProps extends ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>
```

What a `Button` takes.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | field | `ButtonVariant` | How it reads. |
| `size` | field | `ButtonSize` | Its size. |

## Button

```typescript
function Button({ variant = "default", size = "md", className, ...rest }: ButtonProps)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `ButtonVariant` | `"default"` | how it reads: plain, the one action on the panel, the one that destroys something, a warning, or one that should not be the first thing the eye lands on. |
| `size` | `ButtonSize` | `"md"` | its size: `md` unless the row is dense, in which case `sm` or `xs`. |
| `className` | — | optional | added to the element's classes, beside the one the theme gives it. |
| `rest` | — | optional | the remaining props, spread onto the button. |

A button.

The variant is a prop rather than a class name you spell:
`btn-primery` is a typo that renders as a plain button and looks
like nothing at all, which is exactly why the name is one the
compiler checks.

**Also** [`ButtonProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#buttonprops).

## Tone

```typescript
type Tone = "neutral" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"
```

How loud a status is.

`neutral` for a state nothing is wrong with, and the three that
mean something.

## ChipProps

```typescript
interface ChipProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>
```

A tag the reader can scan past.

Bordered, pill-shaped, muted, `--text-sm`. Use it for a filter, a
label, a piece of metadata — something that describes the row it
sits on.

`Chip` and `Badge` take the same props and are not
interchangeable. If the thing you are showing is a *state* that
changes — ready, failed, three unread — it is a `Badge`,
which is filled by tone and bold so it is noticed. If it is a fact
about the thing, it is a `Chip`.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tone` | field | `Tone` | How loud it is. |


| `className` | — | optional | added to the element's classes, beside the one the theme gives it. |
| `rest` | — | optional | the remaining props, spread onto the span. |

## BadgeProps

```typescript
interface BadgeProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>
```

A state the reader is meant to notice.

Filled by tone, bold, `--text-xs`, no border. See `ChipProps`
for which of the two to reach for.

The tone is colour, and colour alone is not a message: put the
state in the text too. "Failed" in a danger badge survives being
read aloud and being looked at by somebody who cannot tell it from
the success one; an empty red badge does not.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tone` | field | `Tone` | How loud it is. |

| `rest` | — | optional | the remaining props, spread onto the span. |

## EmptyProps

```typescript
interface EmptyProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>
```

What to show where there is nothing.

Its own component rather than a paragraph with a class, because an
empty state that says only "nothing here" is the commonest way a
panel wastes the one moment it had the reader's attention. The
`action` slot is a nudge to say what to do next.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | field | `ReactNode` | A button, usually: the one thing to do about being empty. |

## Empty

```typescript
function Empty({ children, action, className, ...rest }: EmptyProps)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | — | optional | what to show where there is nothing. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | optional | a button, usually: the one thing to do about being empty. |
| `className` | — | optional | added to the element's classes, beside the one the theme gives it. |
| `rest` | — | optional | the remaining props, spread onto the element. |

What to show where there is nothing.

See `EmptyProps` for why the `action` slot exists.

**Also** [`EmptyProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#emptyprops).

## DialogProps

```typescript
interface DialogProps extends Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "title">
```

What a `Dialog` takes.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | field | `ReactNode` | Its title. Also the accessible name of the dialog. |
| `sub` | field | `ReactNode` | Shown under the title. A sentence, not a paragraph. |
| `children` | field | `ReactNode` | The body. |
| `actions` | field | `ReactNode` | The buttons. Rendered in an `Actions` row at the foot. |
| `onClose` | field | `() => void` | Escape, or a click on the backdrop. |

## Dialog

```typescript
function Dialog({ title, sub, children, actions, onClose, className, ...rest }: DialogProps)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `ReactNode` | required | its title, also the accessible name of the dialog. |
| `sub` | `ReactNode` | optional | shown under the title: a sentence, not a paragraph. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | optional | the body. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | optional | the buttons, rendered in an `Actions` row at the foot. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | required | escape, or a click on the backdrop. |
| `className` | — | optional | added to the element's classes, beside the one the theme gives it. |
| `rest` | — | optional | the remaining props, spread onto the dialog panel. |

The one primitive here that is behaviour rather than a box.

A dialog has to trap focus, close on Escape, restore focus to
whatever opened it, and not let a click inside the panel count as a
click on the backdrop. Every extension that built its own would get
some of that wrong, and the ones they get wrong are the ones only
keyboard and screen-reader users notice.

**Also** [`DialogProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#dialogprops).

```typescript

```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |

## SwitchProps

```typescript
interface SwitchProps extends Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "onChange">
```

What a `Switch` takes.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checked` | field | `boolean` | Whether it is on. |
| `onChange` | field | `(next: boolean) => void` | Called with the next value. It takes effect at once. |
| `label` | field | `ReactNode` | Shown beside the switch, and used as its accessible name. |

## Switch

```typescript
function Switch({ checked, onChange, label, className, ...rest }: SwitchProps)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checked` | `boolean` | required | whether it is on. |
| `onChange` | `(next: boolean) => void` | required | called with the next value; it takes effect at once. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | required | shown beside the switch, and used as its accessible name. |
| `className` | — | optional | added to the element's classes, beside the one the theme gives it. |
| `rest` | — | optional | the remaining props, spread onto the button. |

A switch, which is a button rather than a checkbox.

The difference is not cosmetic. A checkbox is a value you submit; a
switch takes effect the moment it moves. `role="switch"` is what
tells a screen reader which of those it is looking at.

**Also** [`SwitchProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#switchprops).

## FieldProps

```typescript
interface FieldProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>
```

A label, a control, and room for the reason it is wrong.

The error slot is the part that gets left out, and a form that
rejects input without saying why is the one people abandon. When
`error` is set it is wired to the control through
`aria-describedby`, so it is announced rather than merely shown.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | field | `ReactNode` | The label. It is visible, not a placeholder. |
| `hint` | field | `ReactNode` | A sentence under the control, for when nothing is wrong. |
| `error` | field | `ReactNode` | Why the control is wrong. It replaces the hint while it is set. |
| `htmlFor` | field | `string` | The id of the control, so the label points at it. |

## Field

```typescript
function Field({ label, hint, error, htmlFor, children, className, ...rest }: FieldProps)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `ReactNode` | required | the label, which is visible rather than a placeholder. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | optional | a sentence under the control, for when nothing is wrong. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | optional | why the control is wrong; it replaces the hint while it is set. |
| `htmlFor` | `string` | optional | the id of the control, so the label points at it. |
| `children` | — | optional | the control the label is for. |
| `className` | — | optional | added to the element's classes, beside the one the theme gives it. |
| `rest` | — | optional | the remaining props, spread onto the element. |

A label, a control, and room for the reason it is wrong.

See `FieldProps`. The error slot is the part that gets left
out, and a form that rejects input without saying why is the one
people abandon.

**Also** [`FieldProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#fieldprops).

## SpinnerProps

```typescript
interface SpinnerProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>
```

Work whose duration is unknown. `Skeleton` is for known shapes.

`label` is required for the same reason `Progress.label` is. This
was `role="status"` on an empty span: a live region with nothing
to say, so a screen reader got silence while a sighted user
watched something spin.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | field | `string` | Required: a spinner with no name is a live region with nothing in it. |

## Spinner

```typescript
function Spinner({ label, className, ...rest }: SpinnerProps)
```

|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | required | required: a spinner with no name is a live region with nothing in it. |
| `className` | — | optional | added to the element's classes, beside the one the theme gives it. |
| `rest` | — | optional | the remaining props, spread onto the span. |

Work whose duration is unknown.

See `SpinnerProps` for why `label` is required.

**Also** [`SpinnerProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#spinnerprops).

| `className` | — | optional | added to the element's classes, beside the one the theme gives it. |
| `rest` | — | optional | the remaining props, spread onto the element. |

Tabs with the arrow keys wired, because a tab strip that only
responds to clicks is a tab strip half the people cannot use.

**Also** [`TabsProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#tabsprops).

## TabPanelProps

```typescript
interface TabPanelProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>
```

The panel a tab controls. Needs the same `base` the strip used.

Published because `Tabs` without it is half the ARIA pattern: the
strip announced that it controlled something and there was nothing
for it to control.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base` | field | `string` | The id prefix shared with its `Tabs`, so the two agree. |
| `id` | field | `string` | Which tab this panel belongs to. |
| `active` | field | `string` | Which tab is showing. The panel renders only when they match. |

## TabPanel

```typescript
function TabPanel({ base, id, active, children, className, ...rest }: TabPanelProps)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base` | `string` | required | the id prefix shared with its tabs, so the two agree. |
| `id` | `string` | required | which tab this panel belongs to. |
| `active` | `string` | required | which tab is showing; the panel renders only when they match. |
| `children` | — | optional | the content of the panel, shown while its tab is the active one. |
| `className` | — | optional | added to the element's classes, beside the one the theme gives it. |
| `rest` | — | optional | the remaining props, spread onto the element. |

The panel a tab controls.

See `TabPanelProps`. It renders nothing at all when its tab is
not the active one, so the content of a panel that is not showing
is not in the page.

**Also** [`TabPanelProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#tabpanelprops).

## HeadingProps

```typescript
interface HeadingProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLHeadingElement>
```

What a `Heading` takes.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | field | `1 | 2 | 3 | 4` | The outline level. Also picks the size, so they cannot disagree. |

## Heading

```typescript
function Heading({ level = 2, className, style, ...rest }: HeadingProps)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4` | `2` | the outline level; it also picks the size, so the two cannot disagree. |
| `className` | — | optional | added to the element's classes, beside the one the theme gives it. |
| `style` | — | optional | the element's inline style, merged over the size the level picks. |
| `rest` | — | optional | the remaining props, spread onto the heading. |

A heading, at the level you say.

The size follows the level, so the outline and the type cannot
disagree — which is the whole reason there is no `Title`.

**Also** [`HeadingProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#headingprops).

## TextTone

```typescript
type TextTone = "default" | "muted" | "faint"
```

How loud. Not `Tone`: this is emphasis, not status.

`TextTone` says how loud it is — emphasis, not status. A
